attempts.summary: Built a site-to-site IPsec (IKEv2/ESP, AES256-SHA256) tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) across their transit link (10.10.0.0/30), carrying node3's LAN-A (10.20.0.0/24) and node4's LAN-B (10.30.0.0/24) private subnets. Discovered the real interface topology by ARP-probing unaddressed NICs (node1 eth1=transit/eth2=lan-a, node2 vtnet1=transit/vtnet2=lan-b), configured VyOS natively (set/commit/save) and OPNsense via a generated local API key plus the swanctl model schema (read directly from the on-disk model XML to avoid guessing). Diagnosed and fixed a real OPNsense pf gap: the built-in auto-generated 'pass out on enc0' rule was non-quick and did not reliably permit freshly-decrypted (state-less) forwarded traffic from node3->node4, while state-matched reply traffic passed; added an explicit 'pass in quick on enc0' rule, verified with pfctl -d that pf was indeed the blocker, then confirmed the proper fix restored bidirectional, 0%-loss encrypted connectivity. All four nodes were restarted one at a time (VyOS/OPNsense native reboot, Ubuntu native reboot), boot-identity change confirmed via boot_id/kern.boottime, and full tunnel + end-to-end private-address reachability was reverified after each restart, finishing with a clean bidirectional test after all four restarts.
